articles.headline_raw:
Clarify if migrants who
speak Bengali detained
on suspicion of being
Bangladeshi: SC to Govt
articles.body_raw:
ANANTHAKRISHNANG
NEW DELHI, AUGUST 29

THE SUPREME Court Friday
asked the Centre to respond toa
petition which alleged that
Bengali-speaking migrant work-
ers from West Bengal were be-
ing detained by authorities in
various states on the suspicion
of being Bangladeshi citizens.
The bench of Justices Surya
Kant, Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul
M Pancholi, while acknowledg-
ing that there is a problem of il-

legal infiltration in the country,
asked the Centre to clarify
whether authorities are using a
“particular language” as a “pre-
sumption of the speaker beinga
foreigner.”
Justice Bagchi said, “We
would like you to clarify if cer-
tain bias in respect of the exer-
cise of power by authorities, as
sought to be demonstrated by
this petition, namely the use ofa
particular language as a pre-
sumption of being a foreigner,
whether at all this is correct.”
CONTINUEDON PAGE2
articles.headline: Clarify if migrants who speak Bengali detained on suspicion of being Bangladeshi: SC to Govt
articles.text: THE SUPREME Court Friday asked the Centre to respond toa petition which alleged that Bengali-speaking migrant workers from West Bengal were being detained by authorities in various states on the suspicion of being Bangladeshi citizens. The bench of Justices Surya Kant, Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi, while acknowledging that there is a problem of illegal infiltration in the country, asked the Centre to clarify whether authorities are using a "particular language" as a "presumption of the speaker beinga foreigner." Justice Bagchi said, "We would like you to clarify if certain bias in respect of the exercise of power by authorities, as sought to be demonstrated by this petition, namely the use ofa particular language as a presumption of being a foreigner, whether at all this is correct." CONTINUEDON PAGE2

EIGHT OPPOSITION-ruled "like-minded" states - Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and West Bengal - which met in New Delhi on Friday said they explicitly and unambiguously supported the Centre's GST rate rationalisation proposal, but were concerned about revenue loss. In a joint statement, the states projected revenue loss of

between Rs 85,000 crore and Rs 2 lakhcrore a year and sought "protection of revenue interest and fiscal stability in a federal structure". They said states should be compensated for revenue loss - anythinglower than 14 percent revenue growth - for aminimum five years.
